To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new method was developed for the isolation of three distinct fractions of soybean root nodule symbiont, and the method may be useful for studies of the development, senescence, and physiology of the nodule symbion.
the isolation procedure separates node symbionts into distinct fractions, and the lightest fraction appears to be the bacteroids.
a method has been developed for isolating bacteria, transforming bacteria and bacteroids from the nodules of soybean plants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of the symbiotic bacteria from the root nodules of leguminous plants.
the study of the physiology of the nitrogen-fixing symbiotic association of Rhizobium japonicum with the roots of soybean.
the isolation and identification of bacteria, transforming cells and bacteroids from nodules of soybeans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lightest band is the mature bacteroid, the intermediate band the bacterium, and the heaviest band the transforming bacteria.
the bacteroid is the mature symbiont, the transforming bacterium the immature symbiont, and the bacterium the free-living symbiont.
the bacteroids in the lightest band are mature, the bacteroids in intermediate band are in a transforming stage, and the bacteroids in heaviest band are in a developmental stage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nodule is a complex structure in which a number of distinct populations of bacteria are found.
the bacteroid is a metabolically active, differentiated, and specialized cell type, which is not a mere extension of the host cell.

bacteroids are isolated from the light band of a sucrose gradient and are characterized by the absence of cytochromes, by a low level of NAD(P)H dehydrogenase, and by a high level of succinic dehydrogenase activity, while the intermediate band is characterized by the presence of all three electron carriers and by a higher level of NADPH dehydrogenase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bacteroid population of the soybean nodule is not homogeneous.
we can separate the different stages of the bacteria from the nodule.
we have developed an efficient and reproducible procedure for the isolation of different fractions of nodule symbiont from soybean nodular homogenate.
